packs.title: House tours, galleries and garden paths
packs.promise: Compare admitted collections and house details, write from actual gardens and explore distinct public park settings.

q.s: Separate an object’s visible form from its museum interpretation.
st: Enter the actually opened History Center galleries and choose two displayed objects with public interpretation. No particular exhibition, historic vehicle or work is required.
Record one visible material or form detail for each object. Beside it, paraphrase one statement made by the museum interpretation; identify it as a museum statement.
Compare the records. Write one question or limit that the two objects leave open about the account presented.
Complete two object records, your comparison and question after exit if needed. Use your own words rather than copying a panel or artwork.

q.s: Collect three relationships between form and interpretation.
st: Enter the actually opened museum with any required admission. Choose three displayed works that can be compared through different visible forms, spacing, scale or materials.
For each, write one directly visible relationship and paraphrase one point of its public interpretation. If the interpretation does not answer a question, keep that question open.
Compare two records: how does one visible choice affect what you notice first? No preferred artist, cultural tradition or positive judgment is required.
Finish three records and one comparison after exit if needed. Describe rather than reproduce an artwork, label, face or gallery photograph.

q.s: Collect park details from an ordinary visitor route.
st: Choose an actually open public park path and three different visible forms beside it: one planted form, one built form and one meeting between path and open space.
Describe each through shape, texture or spatial relation. Keep observations on the visitor side of fences and away from play equipment and active sports.
Compare two records: how do they affect movement or where a person might pause? State uncertainty if a form’s purpose is unclear.
Write three form records and a comparison. Collect observations only; leave plants, stones and objects where they are.

packs.title: Civic Center and Old Pasadena paths
packs.promise: Read actual civic and museum details, make original pages and follow bounded public paths.

q.s: Collect relationships explained in one actual gallery.
st: Enter the actually opened Crossroads gallery with any required admission. Find three available displays explaining connections among travel, exchange, materials, ideas or objects.
For each, record one actual displayed detail and paraphrase the connection explained by its interpretation. Do not assume all places or periods shared the same experience.
Compare two records and write one limit or question that the displays leave open. Keep a visible detail separate from a supplied historical statement.
Finish three connection records and a comparison or question after exit if needed. No copied panel, map, image or artwork is required.

q.s: Turn exterior forms into an original stage plan.
st: Observe the actual north exterior from open public pedestrian space. Choose three visible forms, such as an upper window, door rhythm and roof edge.
Make a simple original stage plan on paper or in notes. Assign each of your three forms a fictional entrance, backdrop or change of level.
Give two unnamed fictional characters a beginning position and one movement each. No performance, real person or current show is required.
Finish the plan with three form-to-stage links and the two movements. Write after moving away from the entrance if it is busy.

q.s: Collect how materials meet in actual displayed work.
st: Enter the actual opened visitor gallery, without entering a class, studio or staff area. Choose three visible places where materials meet or change in displayed work.
For each, describe the materials or visible forms without touching them. Paraphrase one related point from the public interpretation if available; record a question when uncertain.
Compare two material meetings. Write how their differences affect what you notice, without assigning the artist a motive unsupported by the display.
Complete three records and one comparison after exit if needed. Do not copy the appearance of a whole work, portrait or exhibition installation.
